topic: Who invented the toothbrush? (history explainer, host Nea Costel)
title: WHO INVENTED THE
TOOTHBRUSH?

script.text: All he has is a bone from his dinner.
And what he makes with it is in your bathroom right now.
Who invented the toothbrush? Not a dentist.
China had bristle brushes over a thousand years ago.
But the one you use? That rioter. William Addis.
The story goes: he drills tiny holes in the bone and ties in bristles.
Out of jail, by 1780, he's selling them.
His company still makes toothbrushes, more than two hundred and forty years later. That's real.
So every morning, you brush with a rioter's idea.

science.claim: Bristle toothbrushes existed in China over a thousand years ago.
William Addis was jailed in 1770 for causing a riot; the story says he made a brush from a bone and bristles; he started production by 1780.
science.working: Bone-from-dinner detail is legend ("the story goes"); company founded 1780.

science.claim: More than 240 years later the company still makes toothbrushes.
